correctness.rationale: For arbitrary fixed 0<x<y<1 the bridge Markov property yields exact piecewise-linear conditional mean and independent local residual bridges. Integration gives estimator (1), Gaussian fourth moments give Var(E[Q|U,V])=2tr[(H Sigma)^2], and Wick/kernel integration yields Var Q=1/45. Direct symbolic matrix multiplication supplies polynomial G(r,t). On 0<=r<=1/4 it is convex in t^2 so maximizers are centered or at a one-observation boundary, the latter below the strict centered peak. On 1/4<=r<1/2 the derivative in r is negative throughout the shrinking feasible strip by a factored endpoint upper bound, hence values are below the peak. Centered derivative has the unique positive interior root (sqrt(41)-1)/40. Continuous limits handle repeated and endpoint sites. The packaged independent segment-integration verifier passed symbolic identities, 325 rational-matrix checks and 5151 finite grid checks; finite tests do not establish the continuum step.

originality.rationale: Compared the exact claim and its implications with the accessible historical and published records. Foster–Lyons–Oberhauser Theorem 2 conditions integrated squared Wiener motion on an endpoint and a path integral, not on two optimally located bridge point evaluations. Published Brownian-bridge kernel quadrature has a linear functional and an iid node law, whereas the new target is quadratic and the pair is deterministic. Earlier local Wiener quadratic-energy optimization changes covariance and has a different asymmetric optimizer; it does not imply the pinned result. Targeted mathematical and published-finding corpus searches did not return the displayed radical pair, risk, or an equivalent two-point fixed-design classification. Priority is provisional because inaccessible older quadratic-functionals literature may contain an equivalent result.

value.rationale: The integrated squared bridge is a natural Cramér–von Mises-type quadratic path energy and a leading nonlinear Wiener functional used in numerical SDE approximation. Given only two function evaluations, the result answers an exact budgeted optimal information-design question, including unrestricted placement, nonlinear optimal estimator, uniqueness and all boundary/collision competitors. Its radical nodes differ strictly from standard trisection sites for the linear integral; the exact risk gain is nonzero. This is a natural complete small-budget classification, not an arbitrary restricted numerical invariant; no claim of broader SDE solver gains is made.
